item.title: Exotic Universal Covers and Free Cyclic Actions from the Cartwright-Steger Surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.28956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we construct a closed minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $35$, and signature $1$. The construction is a genus-five symplectic sum of a blowup of the regular fourfold Cartwright-Steger cover and a cyclic Akhmedov-Park manifold. The gluing identifies the homomorphisms from the two surface groups to $\Z/m$. The universal cover is minimal symplectic and is homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $(18m-1)\CP\#(17m-1)\CPb$. It admits a free symplectic action of $\Z/m$. Intermediate quotients give examples with fundamental group $\Z/n$ and characteristic numbers $(e,\sigma)=(35k,k)$ for every $n\geq2$ and $k\geq1$. Using the same Cartwright-Steger summand, we also construct, for every $m\geq2$, a minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $31$, and signature $1$, whose minimal symplectic universal cover is an exotic copy of $(16m-1)\CP\#(15m-1)\CPb$ with a free symplectic $\Z/m$-action.
item.dc:creator: Anar Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, S\"{u}meyra Sakall{\i}, Sai-Kee Yeung

item.title: Contact rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants
item.description: arXiv:2611.29126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study $C^0$-rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants on closed contact manifolds. We prove that Poisson commutation is closed under uniform convergence, establish weak rigidity for pairs without common zeros, and obtain lower semicontinuity under quantitative control of Reeb derivatives. A three-dimensional counterexample shows that unrestricted weak rigidity fails. For partitions of unity, the contact bracket itself controls the Reeb derivatives. Using monotone homogeneous quasi-morphisms and the Cant--Kilgore--Zhang spectral invariant, we derive positive lower bounds for invariants of open covers and configurations of compact subsets. Applications include a quantitative contact big fiber theorem, bounds on Hamiltonian chord durations and Reeb travel times, and deformations of contact one-forms.
item.dc:creator: Jun Zhang

item.title: Symplectizing stable generalized complex four-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.29572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explicitly describe a surgery that turns a stable generalized complex four-manifold into a symplectic four-manifold. As a consequence, we show that for $n\geq 2$, the almost complex manifold $(n^2+n+1)S^1\times S^3\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ admits no stable generalized complex structures or constant type generalized complex structures. We also prove an irreducibility result for stable generalized complex four-manifolds and we show that the moduli space of generalized complex structures on an elliptic surface has infinitely many components.
item.dc:creator: Gil R. Cavalcanti, Bas Wensink

item.title: A symplectic Hilbert hotel
item.description: arXiv:2611.29607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a smooth global symplectomorphism of an infinite dimensional separable Hilbert space mapping a ball of large radius to a subset of a cylinder of small radius. This symplectomorphism and its inverse map bounded sets to bounded sets. This example shows that Gromov's non-squeezing theorem does not generalize to infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces without further assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Abbondandolo

item.title: Scaling limits for equivariant Szeg\H{o} kernels near a singular point of the moment map and applications to K\"ahler reduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.30311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose that a compact and connected Lie group acts holomorphically on a Hodge manifold, and that the action linearises to the associated Hermitian ample line bundle. Assume that zero is a singular value of the associated moment map. The spaces of global holomorphic sections of powers of the line bundle decompose over the finite dimensional irreducible representations of the group. The main goal of this paper is to study the scaling limits for equivariant Szeg\H{o} kernels near a singular point of the moment map. As an application, we discuss the quantization of the singular reduced space: the behaviour of invariant sections along the singular strata, the failure of the asymptotic unitarity of the Guillemin--Sternberg map near the singular strata, and the number of invariant sections concentrated near a singular orbit.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Galasso

item.title: Equivariant Localization for $K(n)$-Local Gromov-Witten Invariants with Applications to Gopakumar-Vafa Invariants
item.description: arXiv:2611.30975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For certain complex-oriented $K(n)$-local cohomology theories, we establish equivariant localization formulas for global Kuranishi charts and a Riemann-Roch formula. We apply these formulas to compute the genus-zero Gromov-Witten invariants of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)$ at odd primes, obtaining a residue formula in terms of the formal group law of the chosen complex orientation. As an application, we derive a multiple-cover formula expressing the genus-zero Morava $K$-theoretic Gromov-Witten invariants of closed symplectic Calabi-Yau threefolds in terms of their Gopakumar-Vafa invariants.
item.dc:creator: Guangxi Yan

item.title: Quantitative thick-fiber property
item.description: arXiv:2611.31071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the quantitative thick-fiber property, an analogue of the Entov--Polterovich non-displaceable fiber theorem for maps whose coordinate functions need not Poisson commute. We prove that this property holds for closed symplectic manifolds admitting a suitable, not necessarily linear, functional on the space of continuous functions. Conversely, we establish an obstruction and show that the property fails for certain irrational symplectic four-tori and Kodaira--Thurston manifolds. These results reveal a new rigidity--flexibility distinction: whereas the Entov--Polterovich theorem gives a universal fiber-rigidity phenomenon, its quantitative counterpart holds on some closed symplectic manifolds and fails on others, thereby defining a new symplectic rigidity invariant. We also introduce the non-displaceability width of a continuous map, defined as the infimum of the radii for which a non-displaceable thick fiber exists, and use it to obtain quantitative obstructions to uniform approximation by maps with small Poisson brackets.
item.dc:creator: Adi Dickstein

item.title: Correspondence between orbit equivalences and exact symplectomorphisms for Anosov flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.28183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that for a closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, two Anosov flows are orbital equivalent if and only if the corresponding Anosov Liouville structures are exact symplectomorphic.
item.dc:creator: Agustin Moreno

item.title: Certified $p$-adic normal forms: an Eliasson-Vey theorem and zero sets of orbits
item.description: arXiv:2611.29586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: I use the Smith form of the homological operator to construct partial Poincar\'e-Dulac normal forms near an equilibrium of a vector field on $\mathbb {Z}_p^d$ with coefficients divisible by $p$ (by $4$ if $p=2$). Retaining the directions whose removal would cost more than a fixed number of digits gives convergence on an explicit ball for any linear part. For polynomial fields, an exact integer check of the conjugacy defect certifies the computed flow to $K$ digits in rescaled coordinates. When the quadratic parts of an integrable Hamiltonian system at a rank-$0$ point span a Cartan subalgebra, the homological divisors in symplectic eigencoordinates are integers. This lets me use Newton iteration to obtain an exact $p$-adic Eliasson--Vey normal form at every prime and for every Williamson type. In exact linear normal coordinates, a polynomial restricted to an orbit gives a sum of exponentials, to which van der Poorten's bound of $2s-3$ zeros applies for a nonzero sum with $s\ge2$ distinct exponents. For integer orbits of polynomial maps, I combine exact modular orbits, Strassmann bounds and archimedean estimates in an adelic sieve. At every prime, increasing the modular depth eventually excludes a time class exactly when the interpolation along its center-manifold shadow has no zero in $\mathbb {Z}_p$.
item.dc:creator: Kirill Terskii

item.title: Fast growth of periodic orbits, translated points and short Floer bars for contactomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.29621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish arbitrarily fast growth of distinct periodic orbits and geometrically distinct translated points for contactomorphisms of the unit cotangent bundle of a closed hyperbolic surface. The conclusions hold on residual subsets of a nonempty $C^1$-open set and follow from Chaidez's contact blender and localized contact perturbations. For a specified analytically admissible normalized Rabinowitz Floer family on a closed contact manifold with Liouville filling, we bound fixed-window barcode entropy by topological entropy. The proof compares long-bar counts with graph volume through contact tomography and filtered continuation. Under strong translated nondegeneracy, we show that super-exponential translated-pair growth in a compact interior window forces super-exponential growth of short bars born in the surrounding window.
item.dc:creator: Wenmin Gong, Zhiyuan Hu

item.title: Characterizing Ultrafast Processes via Work
item.description: arXiv:2611.29778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider the following cycle for a mean-field system initially in thermodynamic equilibrium: an instantaneous parameter jump, relaxation to the new equilibrium, and a reverse jump. For certain systems and parameter values, the two equilibrium macrostates coincide in the thermodynamic limit. We characterize this matching phenomenon through the work required to perform the cycle. Our main result concerns scalar many-particle mean-field systems under suitable assumptions. In the matching regime, the total work has a non-Gaussian limiting distribution, and the average work per particle tends to zero. Away from matching, the properly rescaled fluctuations of the total work have a Gaussian limiting distribution, and the average work per particle converges to a strictly positive constant. Further motivation arises from a contact-geometric model of thermodynamics, in which matching corresponds to a Reeb chord between two equilibrium Legendrian submanifolds.
item.dc:creator: Bernard Derrida, Michael Entov, Leonid Polterovich, Lenya Ryzhik

item.title: Obstructed Harvey--Lawson cones and logarithmic special Lagrangian singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.30082v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct two exact embedded special Lagrangian germs with the same unique multiplicity-one tangent cone, the Harvey--Lawson cone in $\mathbb C^9$. A quadratic obstruction and a corrected cubic obstruction yield the distinct sharp $C^1$ convergence rates $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1}$ and $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1/2}$, respectively. These rates distinguish the germs under unitary transformations and dilations. We also prove Jacobi nonintegrability of the Harvey--Lawson cones in $\mathbb C^8$ and $\mathbb C^9$, and realize the sharp rate $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1/2}$ at the eight-dimensional cone.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Chun Chen, Chun-Kai Lien

item.title: Topological Frobenius algebras
item.description: arXiv:2209.02979v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define in a graded and topologized setting the notions of unital/counital/biunital infinitesimal anti-symmetric bialgebras and coFrobenius bialgebras and discuss their algebraic properties. We also define in this setting the notion of a 2D open-closed TQFT. We illustrate these structures with old and new examples of geometric origin that arise in contexts as varied as symplectic topology, string topology, manifold topology, and quantum homology. The underlying vector spaces, which are typically infinite dimensional, belong to a class of topological vector spaces known as Tate vector spaces.
item.dc:creator: Kai Cieliebak, Alexandru Oancea

item.title: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
item.description: arXiv:2611.14449v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a formula for the Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple determination of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even degree cohomology. This is then applied to the study of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we analyse the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,q}$ as well as ample divisor complements in orbifold K3 surfaces and Calabi-Yau threefolds, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.
item.dc:creator: Elliot Gathercole, Bogdan Simeonov

item.title: Learning Forced Multibody Dynamics on Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.12627v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce an architecture for learning the dynamics of forced mechanical systems evolving on Lie groups, based on discrete forced Euler-Lagrange equations. The proposed method, termed Lie Group Discrete Forced Euler-Lagrange Neural Network (LieDFLNN), learns mechanical dynamics directly from discrete configuration observations, without requiring velocity measurements. This formulation allows the simultaneous identification of unknown mechanical properties and forcing terms, while ensuring that the predicted configurations remain on the underlying Lie group. We develop explicit formulations for rigid body dynamics on $SO(3)$ and $SE(3)$, extend the framework to interacting multibody systems, and introduce a method for learning unknown control forces when the Lagrangian is known. Finally, we evaluate the method through numerical experiments involving rigid body dynamics, nonlinear external forces, controlled systems, and real-world human motion capture data. The numerical results confirm the advantages of incorporating Lie group geometry and discrete variational structure into data-driven modeling of forced mechanical systems.
item.dc:creator: Martine Dyring Hansen, Marta Ghirardelli, Elena Celledoni, David Martin de Diego, Brynjulf Owren

item.title: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.33261v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a closed manifold is regular. On even-dimensional manifolds we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics with trivial isometry group carrying Zoll families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism. In particular, this applies to all even-dimensional manifolds with a Besse family.
item.dc:creator: Christian Lange
